notes: ACCESS: reached exclusively through the Claude-in-Chrome connector in my own tab (tabId 1961714723); no curl/requests/WebFetch/proxy used at any point. robots.txt read in the tab (https://www.zarahome.com/robots.txt, 5840 chars): User-agent blocks are only HTTrack, Slurp, MJ12bot, proximic, AmazonProductDiscoverybot, AmazonProductBot and a generic '*' rule -- zero occurrences of 'claude' or 'anthropic', so no Claude-specific disallow. The Akamai interstitial that the prior HTTP-based pass had to solve never appeared in a real Chrome session. TREE SOURCE: the site's own category tree API, fetched same-origin from the loaded page with javascript_tool: /itxrest/2/catalog/store/84009900/80290093/category?languageId=-5&appId=1 (storeId 84009900 / catalogId 80290093 / languageId -5 = the ES store/catalog pair confirmed by the prior Home-Decor pass). 719 nodes total. There is a single top-level FURNITURE department, id 1020564154 'MUEBLES' (categoryUrl muebles-todo-n4143), with 34 direct children and NO deeper level -- the furniture menu is genuinely flat, the 'empty'/'EMPTY' children being visual separators in the mega-menu. I also keyword-swept the entire 719-node tree (mueble/silla/sofa/mesa/cama/escritorio/armario/estanteria/aparador/vitrina/taburete/banco/butaca/consola/cabecero/perchero/comoda/libreria/exterior + furniture/chair/desk/sofa/stool/bench/cabinet/shelving/wardrobe/hall/office/outdoor) for furniture nodes filed outside MUEBLES: the only hits were duplicates of MUEBLES nodes reached through room departments (DORMITORIO > CAMAS Y CABECEROS = the same dormitorio-camas-cabeceros-n4166 page; NINOS Y BEBES > MUEBLES = the same ninos-muebles-n1122 page; DORMITORIO > VESTIDOR > Muebles = the muebles-n4104 department landing), so nothing furniture-typed is hidden in another department. QTY METHOD: Zara Home renders NO 'N articulos/productos' header anywhere in its grid (checked the rendered listing directly), so counts come from the site's own listing endpoint /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009900/80290093/category/<internalCategoryId>/product?showProducts=false&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false&languageId=-5&appId=1, taking productIds.length. VALIDATION of that method: I loaded https://www.zarahome.com/es/muebles-almacenaje-n4111 in the tab, scrolled the grid to the end and counted unique product tiles by their ?pelement=<id> parameter -> exactly 22 unique tiles, identical to the API's productIds.length of 22 for that node. (Note: the same response's 'products' object is capped at 10 detail records and 'gridElements' is a layout array of 12 -- neither is a count; productIds/sortedProductIds are the full list and agree with each other.) DRIFT CHECK: every one of the 20 leaf counts was read twice in separate passes minutes apart and every value was identical; each leaf URL was also fetched and returned HTTP 200 with a rel=canonical exactly equal to the URL I recorded and a <title> matching the node (no silent parent-serving). No count is suspiciously round and every count differs by category. DEDUP / WHAT I DROPPED, decided by product-ID set arithmetic on the API's productIds, not by name: the FURNITURE department also carries room-rollup children that are cross-cutting views over the same product-type leaves. Against the union of the 18 adult product-type leaves (258 unique ids), MUEBLES COCINA (kitchen furniture, 19) was 19/19 contained, BANO (bathroom furniture, 22) was 22/22 contained, MUEBLES DORMITORIO (bedroom furniture, 34) was 31/34, MUEBLES COMEDOR (dining furniture, 23) was 20/23 and OFICINA (office, 21) was 18/21 -- all dropped as parent rollups whose children I already record, per the deepest-URL rule. ENTRADA (recibidor-entrada-n4981, 119 products) was dropped for a different reason: only 31 of its 119 products are in the furniture department at all; a name scan of its grid shows wall mirrors, runner rugs, seagrass baskets, hooks and magnetic boards alongside the benches and sideboards, i.e. it is a hall/entryway ROOM landing page, not a furniture category (room name never decides). Also dropped: 'VER TODO' (muebles-n4104 / muebles-todo-n4143, 323 products) as a See-All page per rule 3, and 'VINCENT VAN DUYSEN' (vincent-van-duysen-furniture-n3879) as a designer collection page per rule 3. KEPT despite being room-named, because their populations are genuinely distinct rather than duplicates: EXTERIOR (outdoor furniture, 29) shares only 3 ids with the adult product-type union, and NINOS (kids furniture, 55) shares only 5 -- both are separate product populations, and kids furniture is explicitly in scope. SIBLING OVERLAP checks on the leaves I kept, all minor and all left in place as genuinely different listings: Stools vs Poufs-and-Footstools share 3 of 18; Sideboards-and-Cabinets vs Console Tables share 5 of 9; Couches-and-Armchairs vs Accent Chairs share 0. EXCLUDED BY RULESET, not furniture: everything under DECORACION (mirrors, lamps, vases, candles, frames), COCINA Y COMEDOR (tableware, glassware), DORMITORIO bedding/bed linen, BANO towels and fixtures, FRAGANCIAS, LAVANDERIA, ROPA Y ZAPATOS, MASCOTAS. Storage-vs-furniture line: I kept ORGANIZACION because its 22 products are storage FURNITURE (storage units with shelves, wall storage unit, storage units on wheels, glass-door display cabinet, waiter trolley, step stools, shoe bench) with no baskets or bins; standalone baskets/boxes live in a separate DORMITORIO>VESTIDOR>Organizacion node (bano-cestas-cajas-n4142) which I did not take. Hierarchy is genuinely two levels deep (Furniture department -> leaf), so there are no grouping rows to emit.
